wins: Collected detailed service fingerprints during the single episode, yielding actionable port and banner data for follow-up enumeration.
Maintained consistent reward accumulation even though final success criteria were not met, suggesting useful intermediate progress was achieved.
fails: Failed to convert reconnaissance data into a successful compromise, as indicated by the 0% success rate despite an elevated reward.
Relied on mentor assistance 15 times, demonstrating reliance on guidance rather than autonomous decision-making.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance phases produced useful service intelligence, but exploitation and post-exploitation transitions remain flawed, requiring focused attempts on autonomous action sequences.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Unable to chain initial service enumeration into privilege escalation during the episode, repeatedly stalling after the reconnaissance steps.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 80/443 responds with HTTP headers and web technology banners.
skill_cards.then_action: Run targeted nikto and gobuster scans to identify authenticated endpoints and default files.

skill_cards.if_condition: When SSH port 22 is open and banner indicates OpenSSH.
skill_cards.then_action: Execute enum4linux and ssh-user-enum to list valid accounts and weak configurations.

skill_cards.if_condition: When initial scanning identifies SMB shares without immediate access.
skill_cards.then_action: Use smbclient with anonymous authentication to enumerate shares before moving to exploitation.

memory_ops.reason: High confidence in web reconnaissance results contributing to reward increases.
SSH enumeration consistently provided account data for potential exploitation vectors.
